source.title: SafeSteer: A Decoding-level Defense Mechanism for Multimodal Large Language Models
source.authors: Xin-Yi Zeng; Xue Yang; Jingyuan Zhang; Huan-Qian Yan; Xiang Chen; Kaiwen Wei; Hankun Kang; Yu Tian

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study probes harmfulness scores of generated tokens and compares harmful outputs with refusals, bearing conceptually on V5. It does not apply the original difference-in-means direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports latent-space separability and SafeSteer defense results, but its probe is not the claimed harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, and it does not ablate or add that direction. SafeSteer’s benchmark and ablation results therefore do not test the listed versions. The qualitative decoding comparison between harmful and reject tokens bears on V5.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (SafeSteer). It fits a logistic-regression probe on PCA-reduced prefill hidden states, labelled by input harmfulness, and uses it to rerank tokens. It adds a vector built from SD-image minus CB-text attack centroids. It never derives, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. It never checks whether harm judgment and the refusal decision are encoded separately. Its benchmark results (Tables 1–3) measure its own method. The visualization findings are qualitative descriptions of probe separability, a related construct. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that MLLMs can distinguish harmful from harmless inputs during decoding and that image-based attacks are more stealthy. They claim SafeSteer improves safety by up to 33.4% over baselines without fine-tuning, while keeping helpfulness and inference efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a logistic-regression decoding probe and uses a separate image-versus-text modal alignment vector; it does not find, ablate, or add the claimed refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the harmful-versus-harmless boundary is clear in initial decoding steps but becomes indistinct toward the final step.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA/t-SNE of final-layer prefill states in Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL shows harmful and harmless inputs separated by a margin. Image-based (SD) harmful inputs sit closer to the harmless cluster than text (CB) inputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MLLMs, harmful content delivered via images yields weaker harmfulness representations in the decoder than the same content in text.

fits_no_version.finding: The input-harmfulness probe scores compliant responses to harmful prompts as less harmful than refusals at decoding steps 0–3. Separability fades at later steps (Appendix C).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear harmfulness probes on generated-token states track the model's refusal/compliance stance in early decoding steps rather than input harmfulness.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding an SD-minus-CB centroid difference vector at prefill for probe-flagged harmful inputs lowers SD ASR on MM-SafetyBench. On Qwen2.5-VL, SD ASR is 2.16 with SafeSteer vs 3.11 without MSAV (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A modality-shift mean-difference vector added to image-attack inputs increases refusal of image-based harmful requests.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The claim-relevant evidence is qualitative and visualization-based, with no numerical probe scores or uncertainty estimates reported. The paper does not test causal separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
record.rows_left_out: SafeSteer benchmark scores and component ablations in Tables 1 and 3, and its efficiency results in Table 2, were not extracted as rows because they evaluate SafeSteer rather than the claimed refusal direction or the distinction in V5.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction is derived, ablated or added; no measure of capabilities under such an intervention.

Image-based attacks are said to weaken harmfulness representation, but this is shown only qualitatively with the authors' probe. The paper does not test whether attacks suppress a refusal direction, and does no adversarial training.
No separate harmfulness and refusal representations are identified or dissociated.
The MSAV is meant to transfer text safety to vision, but it is not the refusal direction, and transfer is shown only through ASR of the defense.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only as evidence that LLMs discern harmful inputs. The probe uses 4 principal components and logistic regression; it is not the refusal direction. All claim-adjacent evidence is qualitative visualization with no numbers, and the two models are reported jointly. Benchmark rows were correctly left out as method evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: No causal ablation or addition of a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction; no assessment of whether other abilities remain intact under that intervention.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration of the claimed direction.
No test of whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The study does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions. Its use of principal components and a modality-alignment vector is not such a test.
The study does not establish causally or mechanistically that harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded; it reports a qualitative probe-score comparison.
No transfer test of the claimed refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages as determinants of whether a removable direction exists.

relation.reason: The method relies on the premise that harmfulness is linearly readable from hidden states, and that adding a mean-difference vector at prefill shifts outputs toward refusal. Its preliminary t-SNE observations test neither causal mediation nor the refusal direction itself.

tranche.reason: Defense paper. It builds on linear harm separability (cites Arditi et al. once, as motivation) with a logistic probe on PCA-reduced prefill states and an SD-minus-CB centroid steering vector. It never derives, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction, so its own results don't bear on any version. T6 would be a fair reading too.

source_check.notes: The §3 observations are qualitative PCA/t-SNE plots with no numbers or per-model split. R2 (image attacks sit nearer the harmless cluster) is close to V3, but it uses a different probe and has no projection value, so it is not a test. In authors_conclusion, 'up to 33.40%' (abstract) and 'average 33.4% over baselines' (§5.2) are two different claims. Flattened Table 1 seems to show MM-Vet Acc falling with SafeSteer on Qwen2.5-VL (57.50 to 52.20) and LLaVA (31.00 to 27.60).

reader_labels.reason: The probe assigns harmful and reject tokens different relative scores and positions, consistent with a distinction between harmfulness assessment and refusal; see R3.
